text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- NPI IS NEXT MUTUAL TAKEOVER TARGET

Australian Mutual Provident is considering a two billion stg offer for National Provident Institution, the mutual life insurer, after a failed bid for Scottish Amicable. NPI is in the process of appointing City advisers, either Goldman Sachs or Morgan Stanley, to work on either an auction to sell to the highest bidder or a floatation.
-- GERMANS PLAN TO OUTFLANK SEARS BOARD

German mail order group Otto Versand is threatening to intervene in the bidding for Freemans, the mail order group owned by Sears, by appealing directly to Sears' shareholders if the price offered by Littlewoods is less than it is promising. Otto already owns Grattan in Britain.
-- GEHE TO SELL OFF HOLLAND & BARRETT

Gehe, the German drugs retailer and wholesaler which paid 684 million stg for Lloyds Chemists in January, is expected to announce a 250 million stg disposal plan for three of Lloyds' associated businesses. AAH, the pharmaceutical group whose parent is Gehe, will announce plans to sell off Holland & Barrett, National Veterinary Supplies and Martindales, a specialist pharmaceutical manufacturer.
-- LIBERTY SEVERS LINKS WITH MUJI

Department store group, Liberty, has ended partnership with the Japanese Saison Group, and is to pull out of the four Muji outlets owned by the joint venture. Muji's Japanese owners wanted to expand the chain, however Denis Cassidy, chairman of Liberty, was unwilling to invest.
-- MERCURY MINING TO BE WOUND UP

Less than four months after its launch, the investment trust of Mercury Asset Management, Mercury World Mining, is to be wound up and the proceeds distributed to shareholders. MAM made the decision not to expand the life of the trust because of its poor share price performance.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- PROPERTY GIANT IN 3.2 BILLION STG MERGER MOVE

One of Britain's biggest property companies, Hammerson, is in talks with its biggest rival, MEPC, about a merger to create a group worth more than 3.2 billion stg. The fund manager which has a combined stake of 35 per cent in both companies, PDFM, is encouraging the proposal, which could place the group into the FT-SE 100 index.
-- SOUTH AFRICA FAVOURS UK ARMS DEAL

Britain's two defence-industry giants, British Aerospace and General Electric Company, are in line to win a two billion stg government-to-government military equipment deal with South Africa. Other companies, from Rolls-Royce to small sub-contractors, would gain from the largest overseas defence contract since Saudi Arabia bought aircraft worth 2.5 billion stg four years ago.
-- HORLICK'S FORMER BOSS LASHES OUT AT GREED IN CITY

Soon to retire chairman of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, John Craven, has attacked the culture of the City, saying those who work in the Square Mile are greedy and disloyal. His comments were not directed at Nicola Horlick, who was fired from the bank amid allegations she had been trying to take a team with her to join a rival operation, but reflect Craven's displeasure with defecting staff.
-- CLARKE SCOTCHES FEARS OF RISING RATES

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke has insisted that the economy is not overheating and that fiscal policy is under control, with public sector borrowing heading for an undershoot this year. He also dismissed the idea that interest rates need to rise sharply to curb inflation. He insists there is no parallel between now and 1992, when taxes rose sharply after the election, despite ministerial assurances.
-- C&W FACES RISK OF HOSTILE BID

Cable and Wireless is set to lose its protection from takeovers with the removal of the government's golden share. The American government is exerting pressure for the share removal and the protection then ensures no single shareholder cam own more than 15 per cent in the company. This will also hasten the consolidation of the 700 billion dollar worldwide telecoms industry.
THE OBSERVER
-- LONRHO DRAWS UP PLANS FOR NEW SELL-OFFS

Lonrho has drawn up a secret list of businesses it will sell following the separation of its mining operations from the group's African trading interests. These could include the sale of U.K. subsidiaries, including a Lloyd's insurance broker, FE Wright Group, a building contractor, Sunley Turriff Holdings, and Cramlington Textiles, a maker of sheets and duvets.
-- SEARS SALE FARCE PUTS STRONG'S JOB ON THE LINE

Liam Strong, chief executive of Sears, has been given a month by investors to avoid being fired. They are unhappy about his attempts to sell Freemans, the group's mail order business, which fell apart when buyer N Brown pulled out. If preliminary results on 29 April do not show that Sears' performance can be revived, major institutions say Strong must go.
-- ROVER READIES ITSELF FOR RETURN TO U.S. - BUT NOT FOR SEVEN YEARS

Rover, the motor manufacturer owned by BMW, has said that it will now wait until 2004 to launch a fresh assault on the U.S. car market. The company wants to wait until it can offer a wider range of vehicles. Chairman and chief executive Walter Hasselkus said that a return to the U.S. is not essential to the group.
-- SHARES BRACED FOR FALL AS DOW PLUNGES 140 POINTS

The London stock market is set to suffer a sharp fall after the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged by 140 points on Thursday amid fears that the U.S. Federal Reserve will impose a new interest rate rise on top of the quarter-point increase of last week. Strategists expect the fall in London to be on a more modest scale.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- LGV IN COURT VICTORY OVER 'IDEAS'

A High Court judge has dismissed claims brought against Legal and General Ventures by business consultant George Hoskins over the 265 million stg buyout of McBride, the own-label detergents maker, in 1993. Mr Justice Harman rejected the suit saying that no binding promises had been made while LGV sought City backing for the deal.
-- THAMES ON THE WAY TO INDONESIA

The Indonesian city of Jakarta is expected to announce that it has signed a 400 million dollar deal with Thames Water to manage water supply for the capital. Thames is the majority shareholder in a joint-venture with Lyonnaise des Eaux. The contract will reaffirm Thames' committment to systems management and operation as the core of its foreign business.
-- CHANNEL FIVE IN RATING DISPUTE

Television sources claim that it will take months to get an accurate idea of who is watching Channel Five, as measured by the British Audience Research Bureau. The confusion will lead to a war of words between Channel Five and the ITV companies over whether viewing figures are accurate.
-- TAX CHAOS LEAVES CLAIMS 'ON HOLD'

Tax experts warn that the problems faced by the Inland Revenue over the introduction of self-assessment will lead to thousands of people experiencing delays in resolving outstanding tax matters. They believe that staff have put all claims over previous years "on hold" while they put the new system into operation.
-- WAVERLEY SUSPENDS BRE-X ACTION

Waverley Mining Finance has stopped its legal action against Canadian gold explorer Bre-X, the firm at the centre of a possible metals scandal. Waverley's 49 per cent-owned Australian offshoot Montague Gold has been considering legal action for months, but has now decided to see whether it is worth claiming damages at all.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- NEW LABOUR MAY TRY TO PRIVATISE POST OFFICE

Labour Party frontbenches are supporting plans to privatise the Post Office if the party wins the election. This is set to cause a rift with Shadow Chancellor Gordon Brown's Treasury team who do not want to lose the one billion stg the Post Office will provide to the Government by the year 2000.
-- FORMULA ONE IN HEAD-ON COLLISION

Three racing teams are threatening to sue the FIA, motor racing's governing body, over the distribution of millions of pounds stg from television rights. The dispute could undermine plans by Bernie Ecclestone, the sport's commercial boss, to float Formula One on the London and New York stock markets.
-- ROTHSCHILD NEXT ON PRU'S HIT-LIST

Prudential's successful 2.87 billion stg bid for Scottish Amicable is likely see the group attempting more bids. Top of the list is J Rothschild Assurance, the life insurance company. Peter Davis, chief executive of Prudential, has said that he also wants to buy a building society, possibly JRA, which belonged to ScotAm.
-- LABOUR LINES UP A BAN ON RAILTRACK ASSET SALES

The Labour Party is set to stop Railtrack from selling its property assets and bar it from distributing rental profits if the party wins the general election. Labour transport spokesman Andrew Smith said that he would also stop the privatised company from paying shareholders 500 million stg that it could save on its maintenance programme.
-- CASINO BONANZA HAS HAD ITS CHIPS

The Home Office has admitted that plans for gambling zones in 21 towns have been scrapped, dealing a 500 million stg blow to the casino industry, after refusing to relax gambling restrictions because of the forthcoming general election. The Labour Party has no plans ot reintroduce the Bill and wants a review of the gambling industry.
